summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, and recent MRSA catheter-related bacteremia was admitted for evaluation of persistent blurry vision in her left eye following a venogram under anesthesia and symptomatic hypotension after dialysis. Ophthalmology attributed the visual disturbance to transient loss of accommodation from anesthesia, with expected recovery. Hypotension was managed with IV fluids and reinitiation of midodrine. She developed dysphagia, prompting empiric treatment for suspected candidal esophagitis with fluconazole. Due to IVC stenosis and concern for catheter-related thrombosis, warfarin was initiated. She remained stable, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up in ophthalmology, primary care, and INR monitoring during dialysis.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
